title: arbiter rule file
description: Rules arbiter enforces at every Claude Code tool call. Reference: docs/arbiter/reference.md

disable.description: Rule ids from lower layers to turn off.

pattern.description: Literal or glob (* and ?) matching the whole value, or /regex/flags matched by search.

matcher.description: Every key must match. Command keys and path cannot be mixed.

args.description: Positional args, in order but not necessarily adjacent. A nested list means any of.

flags.description: All of these flags present, compared exactly (--context also matches --context=x).

wrapped_by.description: Runs inside any of these wrappers (sudo, env, aws-vault, op, ...).

env.description: Inline NAME=value assignments; values are patterns.

regex.description: /regex/flags searched in the sub-command's raw text.

path.description: Glob against file_path for file tools, and Bash redirect targets; leading ~ is your home.

piped_to.description: A command matcher for a later stage of the same pipeline, e.g. { cmd: [sh, bash] }.

matchers.description: A matcher, or a list meaning any of them.

id.description: Unique within a layer; a higher layer with the same id replaces it. Convention: <area>/<name>.

tool.description: Tool names this rule applies to (default Bash). /regex/ for MCP tools.

unless.description: Excuses a match on the same sub-command or path.

action.description: What happens when the rule fires (default deny). rewrite is not implemented yet and acts as deny.

to.description: Rewrite target; only with action: rewrite.

description.description: What the rule enforces and why; Claude reads it.

hint.description: What to do instead; Claude reads it.

enabled.description: Default true. false turns the rule off in place; its tests still run.

tests.description: Expected outcome -> inputs (Bash command, or a path for path rules). allow means the rule must not fire.
